 CONTROLLED PROCEDURE / CASE FAMILY 983


     PURPOSE             Convert approved night-shift rows into one exact Calendar event and one pre-shift Clock alarm
                         without using cancelled rows.


 1. Selection rule
 Use only a shift row whose status is exactly approved. Ignore every cancelled row, even when its case identifier or
 site resembles the approved row. Interpret every source timestamp as UTC.

 2. Calendar output on the first Android device
    Field                    Required value

    Title                    {case_id} Night shift - {site}

    Start / end              Copy start_utc and end_utc exactly.

    Location                 {site} Gate

    Description              Shift {shift_id}; lead {lead}; check in at {gate}; approval {approval_code}


 3. Alarm output on the second Android device
 Subtract alarm_lead_minutes from the approved shift start. Create one enabled alarm labelled {case_id} {site}
 check-in. The calculation is performed in UTC; the alarm carries the resulting hour and minute.

 4. Worked approved row
    Source                                              Derived Calendar                             Derived alarm

Night Shift Check-In Policy
                            Operations Scheduling • Effective 1 August 2026 • Time basis: UTC


Purpose
Use this policy with the shift register when a staffing-hold event on the first Android phone must become a
confirmed night-shift event and a check-in alarm on the second phone.

Selection and action rules

  1      Match the source. Match the first-phone event title exactly to source_event_title in shift.csv.
         Do not select a row only because its owner or location is similar.

  2      Honor status. Only a row whose status is confirmed may create an event or alarm. A cancelled or
         hold row produces neither.

  3      Create the shift event. On the first phone use the row’s event_title, start_utc, end_utc, and
         location. Set the description exactly to <shift_id>; owner <owner>; approval
         <approval_code>.

  4      Compute check-in. Subtract lead_minutes from start_utc. Set one enabled Clock alarm on the
         second phone at that UTC clock time, using alarm_label exactly.

  5      Do not duplicate targets. If a task-owned event or alarm with the selected title or label already exists,
         update it rather than creating an extra copy.


Worked example
For a confirmed shift starting at 23:00 UTC with a 20-minute lead, the check-in alarm is 22:40 UTC. The example
illustrates the subtraction rule only; always use the selected register row’s own values.


 Control                Required evidence

 Calendar               One exact selected shift event on the first phone

 Clock                  One exact enabled check-in alarm on the second phone
